standard_prerequisites.name: Associative algebra and ideal conventions
standard_prerequisites.statement: Algebras are associative with a unit, subalgebras share that unit, and the two-sided ideal generated by a subset is the span of all products u s v with s in the subset.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used in lem:three, lem:ideal and lem:comu at source lines 3049-3168.

standard_prerequisites.name: Commutativity criterion for a quotient algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: If the images of a generating set commute in a quotient algebra, the quotient is commutative, so every commutator lies in the kernel.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used at source lines 3066-3079 for the containment of the commutator subspace of O.

standard_prerequisites.name: Centrality of gamma
standard_prerequisites.statement: The element gamma of def:abc is central in Delta, as recorded in the retained definition at source lines 301-330.

core_obligations: Recover the alternative presentation of Delta by generators A, B, gamma from the relations eq:u1-eq:u3, including the explicit expressions for C, alpha and beta in terms of A, B, gamma.
Prove Delta = sum over n of O gamma^n, where O = <A,B>, from the fact that Delta is generated by O and by the central element gamma, and note that this sum is not direct.
Show that the commutator subspace of O is contained in O[A,B]O by proving that the quotient of O by the two-sided ideal generated by [A,B] is commutative.

Extract the membership of [A,B] gamma in the commutator subspace of O from the third relation of the alternative presentation, and combine it with the centrality of gamma to prove that O[A,B]O is a two-sided ideal of Delta.
Complete the reverse inclusion with the graded computation that [O gamma^m, O gamma^n] is contained in O[A,B]O for all m and n, whence Delta[Delta,Delta]Delta is contained in O[A,B]O.

proof_roadmap.step: Alternative generators A, B, gamma and the formulas for C, alpha, beta.
Presentation of Delta by A, B, gamma with the two tridiagonal relations and the third relation involving [A,B] gamma.
Delta is the sum of the subspaces O gamma^n.
The three inclusions controlling commutators and the ideal generated by [A,B] in O.
O[A,B]O is a two-sided ideal of Delta.
Both inclusions proving the equality of the two ideals.

difficulty_reason: The counted statement identifies two ideals of the universal Askey-Wilson algebra: the two-sided ideal generated by the commutator [A,B] inside the subalgebra O = <A,B>, and the commutator ideal Delta[Delta,Delta]Delta (source lines 3123-3131). The forward inclusion is immediate, but the reverse one needs the author's reductions: the sum Delta = sum O gamma^n is not direct (lem:notdir), the containment of the commutator subspace of O in O[A,B]O is proved by passing to the commutative quotient O/R (lem:three(i), source lines 3066-3079), the membership of [A,B] gamma in that commutator subspace is read off the third relation of the alternative presentation (lem:three(ii), source lines 3081-3092), and these must be combined with the ideal property (lem:ideal) and the centrality of gamma to control [O gamma^m, O gamma^n] for all m and n (source lines 3146-3166). Expanding commutators of monomials in A, B, C does not by itself give either inclusion.

compared.statement: The center of the universal Askey-Wilson algebra over a field is freely spanned by monomials in its Casimir and three specified central generators when the nonzero deformation parameter is not a root of unity.
compared.difference: The centre is described there by a basis; the counted statement here describes the commutator ideal and is proved from the alternative presentation, with no use of the centre basis theorem.

compared.statement: Faithfulness of the modular-group action on the universal Askey-Wilson algebra (source label thm:faith).
compared.difference: That task retains the Section 2 and Section 3 material on presentations and on the modular-group action; the counted statement here is a Section 11 equality of ideals with its own proof chain, and it shares no proof span with it.

compared.statement: The explicit universal Askey-Wilson homomorphism into U_q(sl_2) tensor a three-variable Laurent polynomial algebra is injective for nonzero q with q^4 not 1.
compared.difference: A different paper; it studies a homomorphism out of Delta, not the commutator ideal of Delta.
